source_text: ἐστι θυσιαστήριον. Καὶ ἵν' εἰδεῖεν οἱ ἀπόλεκτοι πρὸς ἱερουργίαν, τοῦ θείου θυσιαστηρίου τὸ ὑπερφυὲς ὡς ἐν ἁγιασμῷ, καὶ αὐτοῖς ἀνάπτει τὸ σέβας τοῖς ἱεροπρεπέσιν ἐσθήμασιν. Ἐσταλμένους γὰρ ἱερῶς ἔξω φαίνεσθαι τῆς σκηνῆς, οὐκ ἐφίησιν οἰκονομικῶς. Τὰ γάρ τοι, φησὶν, ἡγιασμένα, μὴ τοῖς ἀνάγνοις ὡμιληκότα, καὶ τὸν ἐξ ὀθνείων ἔχοντα μολυσμὸν, τὸ τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς ἀδικείτω σέβας. Διὰ τοῦτο τὴν σποδιὰν, συγκομίζειν μὲν ἐφίησιν ἐσταλμένους ἱεροπρεπῶς, μεταμφιέννυσθαι δὲ πρὸς τὸ ἔξω φέροντας, καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀποφοιτῶντας τόπων. Κεχρησμῴδηκε δὲ τῷ τοιούτῳ συγγενὲς καὶ διὰ φωνῆς Ἰεζεχιήλ· γράφει δὲ οὕτως· «Καὶ εἶπεν πρός με· Αἱ ἐξέδραι αἱ πρὸς βοῤῥᾶν, καὶ ἐξέδραι πρὸς νότον, αἱ οὖσαι κατὰ πρόσωπον τῶν διαστημάτων, αὗταί εἰσιν αἱ ἐξέδραι τοῦ ἁγίου, ἐν αἷς φάγονται ἐκεῖ οἱ ἱερεῖς, οἱ υἱοὶ Σαδδοὺχ, οἱ ἐγγίζοντες πρὸς Κύριον εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ ἐκεῖ θήσουσι τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τὰς θυσίας, καὶ τὰ ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας, καὶ τὰ ὑπὲρ ἀγνοίας· διότι τόπος ἅγιός ἐστιν. Οὐκ εἰσελεύσεταί τις πάρεξ τῶν ἱερέων, οὐκ ἐξελεύσονται ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς τοῦ ἁγίου εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τὴν ἐξωτέραν, ὅπως διὰ παντὸς ἅγιοι ὦσιν οἱ προσάγοντες, καὶ μὴ ἅπτωνται τοῦ στολισμοῦ αὐτῶν, ἐν οἷς λειτουργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, διότι ἅγιά ἐστιν· καὶ ἐνδύσονται ἱμάτια ἕτερα ὅταν ἅπτωνται τοῦ λαοῦ.» Ἅγια μὲν οὖν καὶ αὐτὰ τὰ ἐσθήματα τῶν ἱερέων, καὶ ἄμικτα τοῖς πολλοῖς. Ἐν νυκτὶ δὲ καὶ ἡμέρᾳ τὸ ὁλοκαυτούμενον· ἀκατάληκτος γὰρ ἡ εὐωδία Χριστοῦ· καὶ αὐτὸς δὲ τῶν ἀγίων ὁ βίος, εἰ ὡς ἐν τρόπῳ νοοῖτο τῷ καθ' ὁλοκαύτωσιν, ἄπαυστον ἔχει τὴν εὐοσμίαν· Χριστὸν γὰρ εὐωδιάζουσιν, τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας ἱερουργοῦντες Θεῷ τὰ ὡς ἐξ ἔργων αὐχήματα. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθὴς ὁ λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Τίνα μὲν οὖν τρόπον τὸ τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως ἔσται χρῆμα, δι' ὧν ἔφαμεν, οὐκ ἀσυμφανές. Πῶς δ' ἂν γένοιτο καὶ λίαν ὀρθῶς καὶ ὁ τῆς θυσίας τρόπος, ἐπιτάττει λέγων· «Οὗτος ὁ νόμος τῆς θυσίας, ἣν προσάξουσιν αὐτὴν, οἱ υἱοὶ Ἀαρὼν ἔναντι Κυρίου, ἀπέναντι τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου· καὶ ἀφελεῖ ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τῇ δρακὶ ἀπὸ τῆς σεμιδάλεως τῆς θυσίας σὺν τῷ ἐλαίῳ αὐτῆς, καὶ σὺν παντὶ τῷ λιβάνῳ αὐτῆς τὰ ὄντα ἐπὶ τῆς θυσίας. Καὶ ἀνοίσει ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κάρπωμα ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, τὸ μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς τῷ Κυρίῳ. Τὸ δὲ καταλειφθὲν ἀπ' αὐτῆς ἔδεται Ἀαρὼν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ. Ἄζυμα βρωθήσεται ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ· ἐν αὐλῇ τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἔδονται αὐτήν· οὐ πεφθήσεται ἐζυμωμένη· μερίδα αὐτὴν ἔδωκα αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν καρπωμάτων Κυρίου. Ἅγια ἁγίων ἐστὶν, ὥσπερ τὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, καὶ ὥσπερ τὸ τῆς πλημμελείας. Πᾶν ἀρσενικὸν τῶν ἱερέων ἔδονται αὐτήν. Νόμιμον αἰώνιον εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν ἀπὸ τῶν καρπωμάτων Κυρίου· πᾶς ὃς ἐὰν ἅψηται αὐτῶν, ἁγιασθήσεται.» Τὰ μὲν οὖν ὁλοκαυτούμενα, τὴν οἱονείπως ὁλοτελῆ καὶ εἰσάπαν ἀφιέρωσιν τῶν ἐξαιρέτως ἁγίων ὑποδηλοῖ· θυσία δὲ, αὐτὴν ὡς ἐκ
pass_a_gloss: CYR: [Untouchable also the divine altar] is. And so that those chosen (ἀπόλεκτοι) for sacred work (ἱερουργίαν) may know the surpassing (ὑπερφυές) of the divine altar as in sanctification, also to the sacred befitting garments (ἱεροπρεπέσιν ἐσθήμασιν) themselves he fastens/kindles (ἀνάπτει) reverence (σέβας). For dressed (ἐσταλμένους) sacredly to appear outside the tent he does not allow, economically/with wise provision (οἰκονομικῶς). For, he says, let the sanctified things, having consorted (ὡμιληκότα) with the impure and having the defilement from foreign things (ὀθνείων), not wrong (ἀδικείτω) the reverence of the holy tent. Therefore the ash to gather (συγκομίζειν) he enjoins dressed sacredly, but to change clothes (μεταμφιέννυσθαι) carrying [it] to the outside and departing from the holy places. Akin (συγγενές) to such he has oracled (κεχρησμῴδηκε) through voice of Ezekiel: and he said to me: the chambers (ἐξέδραι) toward north and chambers toward south, those facing the open spaces (διαστημάτων), these are the chambers of the holy place, in which the priests will eat there, the sons of Zadok, those drawing near to Lord into (εἰς) the Holy of holies; and there they will place the Holy of holies (most holy things) and the offerings (θυσίας) and the [offerings] for sin and for ignorance (ἀγνοίας); because holy place it is. None will enter except the priests; they will not go out from the court of the holy into the outer court, so that always holy may be those bringing (προσάγοντες), and may not touch their vesture (στολισμοῦ) in which they minister, because holy they are; and they will put on other garments whenever they touch the people [Ezek 42:13-14 LXX]. Holy then also the garments of priests and unmixed (ἄμικτα) with the many. In night and day the whole burnt thing (ὁλοκαυτούμενον); for unceasing (ἀκατάληκτος) the fragrance (εὐωδία) of Christ; and the life of the saints, if conceived as in manner of whole burnt offering (ὁλοκαύτωσιν), has unceasing fragrance (εὐοσμίαν); for they give forth fragrance of (εὐωδιάζουσιν) Christ, sacrificing as priests (ἱερουργοῦντες) to God the boasts (αὐχήματα) as from works of the gospel citizenship/way of life (πολιτείας). PALL: true the word. CYR: in what manner the matter (χρῆμα) of the whole burnt offering will be, through what we said, not unclear. How also the manner of the sacrifice/grain offering (θυσίας) might become very rightly, he commands saying: this the law of the offering which the sons of Aaron will bring before Lord, opposite the altar; and he will remove from it with the handful (δρακί) from the fine flour (σεμιδάλεως) of the offering with its oil and with all its frankincense (λιβάνῳ), the things on the offering; and will bring up onto the altar a burnt portion (κάρπωμα), odor of fragrance, its memorial (μνημόσυνον) to the Lord. The remainder Aaron and his sons will eat. Unleavened (ἄζυμα) it will be eaten in holy place; in court of the tent of witness they will eat it; it will not be baked leavened; as portion (μερίδα) I gave it to them from the burnt portions of Lord. Holy of holies it is, as that of sin and as that of trespass (πλημμελείας). Every male of the priests will eat it. Lawful thing eternal into your generations from the burnt portions of Lord; everyone who touches them will be sanctified [Lev 6:14-18 Eng. = LXX 6:7-11]. The whole burnt things then the as it were whole complete (ὁλοτελῆ) and entire dedication (ἀφιέρωσιν) of the especially (ἐξαιρέτως) holy suggest (ὑποδηλοῖ); but offering (θυσία) the life itself as in [col. 825:] part holy and under God.
pass_b_english: Cyril: And so that those chosen for sacred service may know the surpassing holiness of the divine altar, he attaches reverence even to the sacred vestments themselves. For with wise provision he does not allow them to appear outside the tent in their sacred dress. For he means: let not the holy things, after contact with the unclean and carrying defilement from what is foreign, wrong the reverence due to the holy tent. For this reason he directs them to gather the ash dressed in sacred vesture, but to change their clothes when they carry it outside and leave the holy places (Leviticus 6:10–11). A command akin to this was also given through the voice of Ezekiel, who writes thus: ‘And he said to me: The chambers on the north and the chambers on the south, which face the open spaces, these are the chambers of the sanctuary, in which the priests, the sons of Zadok, who draw near to the Lord, to the most holy things, shall eat; and there they shall lay the most holy things and the grain offerings, and the offerings for sin and the offerings for ignorance, for the place is holy. No one shall enter except the priests; they shall not go out from the court of the sanctuary into the outer court, so that those who bring the offerings may be holy always, and may not touch their vestments in which they minister, for these are holy; and they shall put on other garments when they touch the people’ (Ezekiel 42:13–14). So the very vestments of the priests are holy, and kept apart from the common people. And the whole burnt offering burns night and day (Leviticus 6:9–13), for the fragrance of Christ never ceases. And the life of the saints too, if it is understood after the manner of a whole burnt offering, has a fragrance without end; for they give off the fragrance of Christ (2 Corinthians 2:15), offering to God, as priests, what the gospel way of life gives them to boast of, as it were, in works.
Palladius: What you say is true.

Cyril: How the matter of the whole burnt offering stands is not unclear from what we have said. And how the rite of the grain offering, too, may be carried out quite correctly he lays down in these words: ‘This is the law of the grain offering, which the sons of Aaron shall bring before the Lord, in front of the altar. And he shall take from it a handful of the fine flour of the offering, with its oil and with all its frankincense that is on the offering; and he shall bring it up on the altar as an offering by fire, a fragrant odor, its memorial to the Lord. And what is left of it Aaron and his sons shall eat. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; in the court of the tent of witness they shall eat it. It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it to them as their portion from the Lord’s offerings by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering. Every male among the priests shall eat it. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, from the Lord’s offerings by fire. Whoever touches them shall be made holy’ (Leviticus 6:14–18). So the whole burnt offerings signify the complete, so to speak, and entire dedication of those who are especially holy, while the grain offering signifies the life that is holy in part and lived under God.

choices.why: Ezekiel 42:13–14 follows Cyril’s LXX text: where standard LXX has the priests ‘eat the most holy things’, Cyril’s text reads ‘who draw near to the Lord, εἰς the Holy of Holies’; rendered ‘to the most holy things’ to keep the εἰς, so ‘shall eat’ has no stated object, as in his wording.
In Leviticus θυσία here is the grain offering (minchah); rendered ‘grain offering’ throughout this passage.
κάρπωμα rendered ‘offering by fire’; πλημμέλεια ‘guilt offering’.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

PG 68.824. The opening words ἐστι θυσιαστήριον complete the last sentence of section 21 and are rendered there. Cyril’s ‘he says’ before ‘let not the holy things…’ introduces his own paraphrase of the law’s intent, not a quotation; rendered ‘he means’. ‘Change their clothes when they carry it outside’ is Lev 6:11 (LXX 6:4). Ezekiel 42:13–14 follows Cyril’s LXX text: where standard LXX has the priests ‘eat the most holy things’, Cyril’s text reads ‘who draw near to the Lord, εἰς the Holy of Holies’; rendered ‘to the most holy things’ to keep the εἰς, so ‘shall eat’ has no stated object, as in his wording. ‘May not touch their vestments’ is literal; the sense is that the vestments must not come into common contact. ‘Night and day’ for the whole burnt offering alludes to Lev 6:9–13 (‘all night until morning’, and the fire kept burning continually); cited as the passage. ‘They give off the fragrance of Christ’ echoes 2 Cor 2:15. In Leviticus θυσία here is the grain offering (minchah); rendered ‘grain offering’ throughout this passage. κάρπωμα rendered ‘offering by fire’; πλημμέλεια ‘guilt offering’. Lev 6:14–18 English = LXX 6:7–11. The first words of col. 825 (μέρους ἁγίαν καὶ ὑπὸ Θεῷ ζωήν) are rendered at the end of this section so the sentence is whole.

changes: τὸ ὑπερφυές: ‘surpassing holiness’, dropped added ‘all else’
Ash-gathering in sacred dress + change of clothes now cited Lev 6:10–11 (was 6:11)
ἄμικτα τοῖς πολλοῖς: ‘kept apart from the common people’ for calque ‘not mixed with the many’
‘night and day’ now cited Lev 6:9–13 (6:9 alone says only ‘all night’; 6:12–13 the perpetual fire)
Rewrote stiff ‘the things they can boast of from the works … of the gospel way of life’
Lev 6:14–18 quote: ‘a handful of’, ‘the Lord’s offerings by fire’; LXX 6:7–11 checked
Ezekiel 42:13–14 checked against LXX; Cyril’s εἰς reading kept as translated (see translator_notes)
